captions.instagram:
Own a rental? Repair or improvement decides how much you write off this year.

✔️ Repairs keep the property in working order: a leaky faucet, a patched wall, paint between tenants. Generally deductible in the year you pay.
✔️ Improvements make it better, restore it or adapt it to a new use: a new roof, a full kitchen remodel, an added bedroom. These are depreciated, and for a residential rental that means over 27.5 years.
✔️ Keep invoices that say what the work was. A vague "repairs" line is hard to defend.

Doing work before Dec 31? Sort it first.
Send this to a friend who owns a rental.

Source: IRS Publication 527. General information, not advice for your situation.
captions.youtube_title: Rental Property: Repair or Improvement? (Deduct Now vs 27.5 Years)
captions.youtube_description: Repairs that keep a rental in working order (fixing a leak, patching a wall, repainting) are generally deductible in the year paid. Improvements (betterments, restorations or adaptations such as a new roof, a kitchen remodel or an added bedroom) must be capitalized and depreciated; residential rental property is depreciated over 27.5 years under GDS. Keep invoices that describe the work. Source: IRS Publication 527.
